ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. quickly

3. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

5. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

6. When practising Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

8. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

9. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

12. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. B — run

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

4. D — Where is the library?

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

11. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
